utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, I would just repeat what I was saying. That Mr. Karadzic said, at page 14788: "Well, in the diary that we just looked at a little while ago, if we had time, we would point your attention to where it says that they had not had contact for 45 days with the representatives from Prijedor." Your Honour, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 23157. Your Honour, this is the conversation that Mr. Karadzic was referring to -- not a conversation, a notation in the diary, and he had previously said that it was his handwriting. And this is at page 14783. When the handwritten document came up on the screen, he said: "This is a session of the Cabinet on the 14th of September, 1992, in Bijeljina." We can see that on page 1. Can we see the next page in Serbian: "This is obviously my handwriting and my diary." And there was only a limited number of the diary -- pages of the diary in evidence, and I seek to use the remaining -- the entire diary now as Exhibit 65 ter 23157. And if we could please go to the ERN, which is R066-3937. And this is a note of -- a notation on the 19th of October, 1992, and I think it says there -- and I'm sorry, Your Honour, we don't have a translation at the moment. It's been put in for urgent translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: There's a meeting of the Presidency and the Main Staff of the RS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the VRS. Yes, the Main Staff of VRS and the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then it says there's a report from Geneva?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then on the next page, does it say "Presidency with Prijedor" underlined?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then: "The first 45 days of the war, there was no connection with us"?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "Problems of the functioning of government and the relations between party and government"?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "Assembly session to be held"?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "Political goals in the army can be interpreted only by SDS members"?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And according to Mr. Karadzic, it's -- he understands the war to be beginning at the beginning of April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the way he's been counting the months of the war, that's my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I seek to tender this document, Your Honour, MFI, marked for identification, and to have a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, let us be precise. The war in Prijedor began in end May, not in April. And, second, am I writing here what I am saying or what I'm being told? How can anyone ascribe to me words which other people tell me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If necessary, the Chamber can give you another go, but it's not for you to intervene with the examination of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just make a point. Mr. Karadzic can't have his cake and eat it too. He either has been putting to this witness throughout her testimony that the war started -- for example, if we have a document at the end of -- end of June, he'll be saying, Well, this is three months into the war, and this is what's happening in Kotor Varos, when, in fact, everyone knows that the war broke out in Kotor Varos on the 11th of June. So he can't, for one minute, be saying three months into the war, in relation to Kotor Varos, and then, in relation to Prijedor, well, it's at the end of May, so now we've got to count 45 days from the end of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It may depend. In any event, what's the number under which we admitted part of this diary?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That was Exhibit D01356, and that was the decision of the Cabinet on the 14th of September, 1992, Your Honour. But this document -- this handwritten diary is a lot longer and covers a lot more period in 1992, and so I thought it was better that we had a new exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark for this --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And may I ask Madam Sutherland to show to the Trial Chamber the entire page, everything that is written on it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We mark this for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P2716, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I want to just quickly, very quickly take you back to the excerpts on the 26th of April, 1992. In your evidence-in-chief, I called up Exhibit D407 because that was the document that we had exhibited in the case, and that was at transcript page 14529. However, in -- during your cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic also brought up Exhibit D407, and that was at transcript page 14774 to 14775. And at that point, you said this is a Latin script and you were using the Cyrillic version; is that right? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have, first of all, quickly on the screen Exhibit D407.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that was the document that you were taken to by both myself and Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if I can now have on the screen Exhibit -- sorry, 65 ter 00783.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is actually the document -- or is this the document that you were referring to --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- and cited in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I used this version in my report, and certainly the one to which I'm more familiar. But I have seen the Latin script, but this is the one I usually use.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, 65 ter 00783.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2717, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if we can just go to the second page of the B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And we can see there that it's got a signature block and a date of the 26th of April?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, you were also asked in cross-examination about the Agency for Resettlement, and that's at transcript page 14640 to 14642. Mr. Karadzic took you to Exhibit D01308, which is the ARK Crisis Staff decision, signed by Brdjanin, of the 26th of May, 1992, where he said, at item 6: "An agency shall be established immediately that will work on the problem of population resettlement." Mr. Karadzic said: "Is that what you meant? Were you referring to agencies of this kind when you said that we oversaw -- or, rather, that the crisis staffs oversaw the removal of non-Serbs?" And you answered: "What I see in a great many municipalities is an institution named variously Property Exchange Agency or Agency for Movement of Population, and so on." And then you go on a little. And then Mr. Karadzic said: "This is what you're reading into this, but this was not done, this was not implemented. You don't know that, but this was not implemented." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 05485 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a decision dated the 12th of June, 1992, of the ARK Crisis Staff to found an agency for population movement and exchange of material wealth for the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Is that the document that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was referring to such agencies at the municipal level as well as this one at the regional level, but, yes, I knew that the -- the item in the ARK conclusions had been implemented, and this is the evidence that I was thinking of, of its implementation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2718, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 05484 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Again, this is a decision of the ARK Crisis Staff, dated the 12th of June, 1992, a decision to appoint Professor Milos Bojinovic from Glamoc as chief of the Agency for Population Movement and Exchange for Material Wealth for the ARK. Were you aware of this decision?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that someone had been appointed. I didn't remember the name. I don't know if I've seen this exact appointment, but I do know that the agency was set up and personnel were named to it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'd seek to tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2719, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I'm now going to show you a number of documents related to this agency. If I could have one moment, Your Honour. Sorry, Your Honour, I've got a lot of paper on my table. While we're waiting for the list to print: Ms. Hanson, on another matter, Mr. Karadzic asked you this morning how many municipalities you had looked at in relation to the documentation for your report, and he named off maybe a dozen municipalities and then asked you, How many municipalities were there, 55 or 60 rather large municipalities, and then said that you probably only included a third or something of that region in your report. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the reference for that, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's today's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Page --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- 13. Thank you, Your Honour. I had it on page 12 and 13, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do recall the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that it was -- it's probably more in the vicinity of 60 municipalities that are listed in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am quite prepared to believe that. I haven't, as I said, made a list of that, but I know it was a lot more than 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I have my piece of paper back in relation to the Autonomous Region Agency for Population Movement. If I could have 65 ter 23145, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did I receive a wrong interpretation or translation? Madam Sutherland said "the displacement of population," and in our language, when this is translated the way it was translated to me, it has a totally different connotation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I said the Agency for Population Movement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, you can see on the screen here a payroll for July 1992, and listing a number of persons. One is Milos Bojinovic, who we've just seen from the previous two documents was a director of the -- appointed director of the agency or as the chief?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What does this document signify to you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It signifies to me that Milos Bojinovic was actively working in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And do we see -- can you make out the stamp at all?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it could be enlarged. I'm afraid I can't see it that well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can enlarge further. We can collapse the English part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see the words "for resettlement" or "movement," and the "Autonomous Region of Krajina, Banja Luka." I can't -- yes, "The Serbian Republic of BiH, Autonomous Region of Krajina," something, "movement," or "resettlement."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: There's a better stamp on the next document. Your Honour, I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2720.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can have 65 ter 23146 on the screen. My apologies, I will slow down. 65 ter 23146.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The English on the screen is a payroll for December 1992, and it is signed by the director, and it has a stamp. And if we could just quickly blow that stamp up.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the Agency for Movement of ARK in Banja Luka, so this would suggest to me that the agency was active and its members were working in December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2721, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 23147 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is an authorisation dated the 10th of August, 1992, signed by Director Milos Bojinovic, and it's entitled "An Agency for Helping in moving of Population and Exchange of Material Property." And it's authorising Ms. Perka Bandic, Mr. Milan Segrt, Mr. Slobodan Bandic, and they're authorised by the government of the ARK and the management of the agency that they can carry out negotiations with the representatives from the Republic of Croatia regarding the matters concerning moving of population and exchange of material property. What does this document signify to you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It signifies to me that the agency was established, was operating, was actively involved in the movement of -- organising the movement of population out of Bosnia altogether, since they're dealing with representatives from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2722, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 23148.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, again, this is a certificate signed by the director, Milos Bojinovic, in relation to an exchange of apartments in Zagreb with one in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it appears.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it's dated the 26th of October, 1992. So did this signify that this agency is working at that point?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2723, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 23150.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This a document dated the 29th of August, 1992, from the Agency for Aiding relocation of Inhabitants and Exchange of Material Assets, and it's a contract on co-operation. It's signed by Perka Bandic and a company in Zagreb. And we saw a moment ago Perka Bandic having authorisation to deal with Zagreb. What does this document signify?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it's organising a convoy of -- from Zagreb -- from Banja Luka to Zagreb, four buses, each taking about sixty people. So it indicates the agency is actively involved in organising the relocation of inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have another five documents relating to the agency. I don't want to waste a lot of time -- not "waste a lot of time," but valuable time going through these documents, and I wonder whether we could simply call them up, and then I could tender them either as a bundle or individually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, we didn't have enough time for our own examination, even with a lot of extensions, particularly a lot of documents. Our own documents we had for this region we chose not to use because of lack of time. So I think if they want to admit a document, it ought to be presented to the witness, and there might to be some thought for allowing Dr. Karadzic some time for re-examination also.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 23 -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We think that Mr. Robinson's comment is fair enough, so let's deal with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a notice in relation to a convoy to Travnik on the 6th of October, 1992. What does this document tell you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it's arranging a convoy to Travnik, which was then Bosnian-held territory, and that each passenger must pay 14.000 dinars to cover the costs of their ticket. So it tells me the agency is actively involved in relocating people.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have -- I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit P2724.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2725, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 23154. I'm sorry -- yes, 23154.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is from the same agency, dated the 1st of October, 1992, signed by the director, Milos Bojinovic, to the CSB Banja Luka. What does this document signify?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're requesting the police to escort a convoy going from Banja Luka to Vlasic. So the agency is actively involved in organising the movement of population.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P2726, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 65 ter 23152, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 13th of November, 1992, again from Milos Bojinovic to the CSB. And is it also requesting an escort from the CSB to assist the convoy?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's very similar to the previous document. It shows that it's a regular -- that this is what the agency is doing, creating convoys, organising their security.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the route is Banja Luka --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Galica-Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Exhibit P2727.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 23156.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 12th of November, 1992. It's signed by the director of the agency to the Secretariat for National Defence, Banja Luka, requesting a war schedule for four individuals. What's the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it describes the employees at the agency, which tells us the agency is working, and that their work in the agency is to be considered as war assignment, and, therefore, that they should not be drafted, but that this assignment is helping the war effort is how I understand that "ratni" [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, finally, if I could have 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it as Exhibit P2728.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. If I could have 65 ter 23155.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is a document dated the 25th of November, from the agency, in relation to services provided by it. And if you could just briefly tell the Court what that -- what those services are.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're organising bus travel, they're organising the moving of furniture, they're organising convoys of private vehicles, and exchanging apartments, making contracts, acting as a middleman between those who are exchanging apartments and other assets.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2729, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, also at footnote 172 of your report, relating to paragraph 100, you cite five municipalities where committees for immigration, travel agencies and exchange officers were established by crisis staffs, and you list Bosanski Petrovac, Kljuc, Kotor Varos, Sanski Most and Zvornik. Your Honour, as these are footnoted in Ms. Hanson's report, I would seek to tender the three that are not yet in evidence. The first one, Petrovac, is Exhibit D01343, and the Kljuc one is Exhibit P02606, but I would seek to tender the one from Kotor Varos, 65 ter 4203 and 00344, and from Sanski Most, the two documents, 65 ter 001 -- I'm sorry, 01097 and 05121, and from Zvornik, 65 ter 11256.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you give the numbers of the first two about the Bosanski Petrovac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Petrovac was D01343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it different from that is noted in her footnote?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, it's the same, 65 ter 01114. That's the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And what is your tendering now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I don't seek to tender that because it's already Exhibit D01343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the next one from Kljuc, that's 65 ter 00853. That's already Exhibit P02606.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now I understand it. Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'm sorry to ask that you take up the time, but I believe that you've already indicated that these documents should not be the subject of -- that you prefer to hear oral evidence. This is almost an oral Bar Table motion, as I understand it, and I don't think it's appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fair enough. Ms. Sutherland, as you noticed, it has been our practice, if the Prosecution finds it necessary to tender the document through a witness, you better put it to the witness. It's up to you, whether or not to put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I could have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you, Your Honour. If, then, I could have 65 ter 04203.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, this is an excerpt from the 14th session of the War Presidency of Kotor Varos of the 14th of July, 1992. Could you briefly tell the Court --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- about this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cite the second bullet point under item 2: "Activities relating to moving out the population failed to meet expectations. This task must be dealt with in a much more organised fashion. An agency has to be established to handle these matters." I cite this as an example of an agency and, in general, of the War Presidency involving itself in the organisation of the moving of population -- the moving out of population.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2730, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 00344.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: These are the minutes of the 37th session of the War Presidency of Kotor Varos, dated the 27th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the bottom of page 1 in English, the War Presidency has received a report on population resettlement and wants a detailed work plan of the Population Resettlement Service, so it suggests to me that an agency has been established and it's reporting to the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2731, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 01097.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is from Sanski Most. It's the conclusions of the Sanski Most Crisis Staff, dated the 23rd of June, 1992. Could you please point out the relevant passage in this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's citing, in fact, that ARK decision -- ARK conclusions that we saw, discussing that, among other things, the army has to be in the line with the SDS. But particularly item G, excuse me, at the bottom of the page -- the English page, that they are faxing -- all municipalities are to appoint a representative on the matters of relocation and exchange of population and prisoners, and they should be faxing these appointments to Vojo Kupresanin, member of the ARK and of the SDS Main Board. And Sanski Most here appoints Vlado Vrkes to that duty. As we recall from a previous document, Vrkes was the one appointed to implement the policies and ideas of the SDS. They've also established a camp at Sitnica. I think I've used this decision for several things but the relevant here is appointing -- implementing the ARK conclusion on agencies for resettlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And also, I'm sorry, item 4, the bottom of the second page of English, the commission, itself, is formed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2732, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 05121.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is minutes of a meeting of the War Staff in Sanski Most of the 21st of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1 is a report of the commission for the movement of population, or the Population Resettlement Commission here in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2733, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And 65 ter 011 -- oh, sorry, 11256.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is a decision on the establishment of the Agency for Exchange of Real Estate Property, dated the 11th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zvornik, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2734.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there a question arising from this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was an agency for exchange of real estate property set up in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I take it to be the case. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Footnote 173 of your report cites to the Bosanski Petrovac document re. the War Commission, and this document was put to you by Mr. Karadzic at transcript page 14749 to 14750. It's dated the -- it's 65 ter -- it does have an exhibit number, but the 65 ter number is 1115.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1344.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And he was saying to you that: "You were treating this document as if ethnic cleansing is the intention of the Serbian authorities to cleanse Muslims from Petrovac; correct?" And you said: "I don't use the word 'ethnic cleansing' or even 'cleansing,' but I say that their solution to -- that -- I say that their solution to Muslims wanting safety was to move the Muslims out. And that was one of the things that crisis staffs did, or war commissions in this case, was organise the departure of Muslims, and this is an example of it." And then Mr. Karadzic said: "Why didn't they just drive them out immediately?" And you said: "As I said repeatedly, Petrovac was a Bosnian Serb majority, and in general, the Serb authorities may have felt they could control the power sufficiently." And then you go on. Were you aware of any convoys being organised for the non-Serb population of Petrovac from mid-September 1992 onwards?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not right now recall seeing documents of such convoys. But I've looked at a lot of documents, so I can't say one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll resume at 10 past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we go to private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I can have Exhibit -- sorry, 65 ter 00242 on the screen, and if you could go to page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you suggested that you would put to the witness a demographic map?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: She's in the position to answer those questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. The document speaks for itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, very well. We'll see.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- and I have some questions. Page 312.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask, is this a document drafted in Croatia about the population of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and was there a census made at the time? In which way is this document relevant to us? This is April 1995. A different state is making assessments about the ethnic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just refrain from making comment at this moment. And when she tenders the document, you have an opportunity to object to the admission of the document. Let's hear from what the witness can say about this document. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So we have on the screen in front of us the ethnicity map for the municipality of Petrovac, which is -- the source document is the 1991 census. And this document has been produced in Croatia in 1995, based on the 1991 census data. And we can see, for the municipality of Petrovac, that it has a total population of 15.621, of which 11.694 are Serb ethnicity, 3.288 are Muslim. Given the population of the Muslims, is it right that having seen the previous document, that by the end of September 1992, basically, the majority -- nearly all of the Muslim population had left the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Objection. Leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So what is your question, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Given what we can see on the screen here, and given the previous document, is it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The first question to be put is whether she agrees with these statistics, if you are minded to ask that question, given the population of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, you said earlier on in your testimony that the Bosanski Petrovac municipality was -- I don't know whether you used the word "Variant A municipality," but you said that it was a Serb majority. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said it was one of the most Serb municipalities, in that it was one of the municipalities with the highest percentage of Serbs. And I'm familiar with this census of 1991. I'm familiar with this publication as a reliable representation of the census. So, yes, I'm familiar with -- these census figures appear correct to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. And then, secondly, looking at the figures here, and bearing in mind the last document, would it be right to say that the majority of the population had left the municipality by the end of September?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority of the Muslim population --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- had left the municipality, yes. If we could look at the map, to just scroll down, I had said that, I believe, the Muslims of Petrovac -- of the municipality were concentrated in the town, itself, and the map shows only two other significant Muslim settlements. So this corresponds with my understanding of the ethnic structure of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I don't know whether you want just this one page. I think it would be helpful for you to have the entire census data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit this page. Do you have an objection, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would not object to this page -- sorry, I'm waiting for the interpretation. I would not object to this page if the figures are correct and if the chart is correct. But I don't see where it shows that the population was moved out and how Croatia established that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It may all go for -- go to the issue of weight which is to be assessed later on. We'll admit this page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The actual figures are on the ERN page 0048-1977 to 0048-1978. It has the municipality total and then it has the breakdown of every village in the municipality. If we could quickly go to 0048-1977. Your Honour, you can see it's got the figures for several different years. And then over on the following page, if you follow "Bosanski Petrovac" along, I think it's number 36, and then you pick up number 36 on the next page, then you see, in 1991, the figures that I just called out, 15.621, consisting of 3.288 Muslims and 11.694 Serbs. So that's where the figures come from for the ethnic map at the back of the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Shall we admit those two pages?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or three pages?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With my objection -- or, rather, with the proviso that the 1991 census is not official, it was not verified before the Assembly, because we had major objections concerning falsifying, which doesn't mean, necessarily, that this is an inaccurate result.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As I indicated, it's a matter that goes to the weight. We'll admit these three pages.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2736, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I take it there are English pages corresponding to these.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: There's English pages for the heading --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Can we see -- can we scroll down to see what it says about the Croatian population originating from Bosnia-Herzegovina, just to see the figure? Can we see the top of the page? Could we maybe zoom in?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this is going to take time, I would mark it for identification, and the accused can -- and look at this volume at his leisure. And then we can come back to the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tell the Trial Chamber that it says: "Population of Croatia originating from Bosnia-Herzegovina, broken down by settlements." How is this relevant, and what does this mean? "Croatian population originally from BH."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We admitted this page to support the page we saw in relation to the map. We'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we were also looking at the figures on the left-hand side of the screen, not the right-hand side of the screen, on that particular page, 0048-1978.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So, Ms. Hanson, Mr. Karadzic took you yesterday to a document -- or Wednesday to a document dated the 28th of October, 1992, from the War Presidency of Bosanski Petrovac, and that was at transcript pages 14753 to 14754, which stated that all Muslims were afforded all rights under the Constitution and for the Public Security Station to increase the patrols. Given the state of affairs by the end of September, this decision by the War Presidency would be affecting a small handful of people, would it not?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is, again, leading and inaccurate. I mean, it's leading, and we'll prove that it is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You preempted Mr. Robinson's role. Yes, that was leading, yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In footnote 174 of your report, you cite three examples of crisis staffs setting the conditions for departure. And you cite documents from Bosanski Novi, Kljuc and Sanski Most. I won't take you to those documents now. But the accused also raised the issue of voluntariness and suggested that the non-Serbs were leaving of their own volition, and then spoke to you about convoys at transcript page 14689 to 14690, and talking about, you know, resettling the population in the areas where they felt safe and whatnot. And you replied that as for the obligation to secure the convoys, you did see lots of documents of municipal authorities securing the convoys you can but not an equal attention was paid to the local population in-situ, the non-Serbian population, that is. Do you recall now what documents that you had in mind when you said that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had in mind documents of the sort we've seen today, arranging the police escort. The crisis staffs often note that they have to get the city transport company -- to get the buses and the police to provide the security, but I did not see them discussing, Can we use those same municipal resources to persuade these people not to move, to make them feel safe. That's what I was talking about, like when the delegation of Muslims comes to the Petrovac War Commission, they ask, Can you make us safe? And the answer is to move them out in an organised fashion, the safety seems to be in -- while they're being moved, but not while they're in place in the municipality, or being -- they're not -- neither are they offered another place in the municipality that might be safer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I now want to move to the municipality of Bosanska Krupa, if I can. And Mr. Karadzic took you to a document at transcript page 14769 to 14772, which was Exhibit D01353, and it was the document of the 1st of May, 1992, from the Committee of Refugees, stating that it's a temporary evacuation of residents and refugees from Arapusa and that the Command is obliged to ensure the safe return of the residents to their homes. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could just take to you a couple of documents now, and I'll ask you to comment. If I could have 65 ter 19898, please. Oh, sorry, before that, 65 ter 06724, and this is the War Presidency order of the 28th of April, 1992, to evacuate the Muslim population from Podgrmec enclave, and using the words "Evacuating them." And in the direction of Bunja [phoen] Japra, Kamengrad and Fajtevci --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fajtevci.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry for my pronunciation. And that's cited in footnote 170 of your report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you cited this document for which reason?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another example of organised evacuation. As I noted, the president of the War Presidency, himself, said that the War Presidency suggested two options to the Muslims; either to organise their own evacuation from the area or to have that effected by military means. So I cite this to support that, in fact, they did carry out these evacuations, and that if the options are merely, Do it yourself or the army will make you move, it can't be considered truly voluntary evacuation. We also have the deputy from Krupa saying in the Assembly that he hopes the Muslims will not come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2737, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And could I please have 65 ter 19898.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, this is a list entitled "List of inhabitants of Arapusa deported to Sanski Most municipality," on the 1st of May, 1992, at 1530 hours. And if we could quickly scroll through the pages, Mr. Registrar. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I have. All the names appear to be Muslim, just on a quick glance. There are so many obviously family -- surnames, and the first names all appear to be Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's a list of 390 names. Is this consistent with what you say in your report in relation to the temporariness of the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a list of 390 persons who were deported from Arapusa municipality to Sanski Most Municipality on the 1st of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what is the provenance of the document? Who did it come from, who issued it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's been provided by a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think we need to know more than that, Mr. President, before you can admit it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can provide that information to the Defence. If we can mark it for identification at this stage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't agree with that. Anyone could have brought this. It has no authenticity at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view that you have another opportunity to tender this document through another witness, so we'll not admit this through this witness at this time. Before you proceed, I'm going to ask you, at the end of your re-examination, to identify the items that you wish to tender among the Appendix B list. So could you identify those --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've done that already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You already have. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 13197 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I cite it in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And unfortunately, Your Honour, we don't have a translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So could you please read the text of the document? Sorry, it's dated the 13th of July, 1992, and it's a War Presidency order.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We're not getting a translation/interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, could you repeat? We don't have the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've taken my headphones so I don't hear the B/C/S -- "[Interpretation] The War Presidency of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanska Krupa is issuing the following order: "The Public Security Station of the Serbian Municipality Bosanska Krupa is hereby instructed to invite, for security reasons, for an interview all persons from mixed marriages and to offer to them, if they so wish, to move out of the area of the Serbian Municipality Bosanska Krupa individually or together. "This order enters into force immediately."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is this consistent with a temporary evacuation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It suggests that people from mixed marriages are still in Krupa in July and that they are going to be -- have it suggested by the police that they might want to leave, which strikes me as a method of intimidation. Perhaps they genuinely want to leave, but if the police are saying that, Because you're in a mixed marriage, you might want to leave, it suggests intimidation to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI 2738, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I'm just a little slow in my thinking about that, but I would like to object to that last answer as beyond the qualifications of this witness as an expert. I don't think that she's in a position to determine, from a document like this, whether -- which, on its face, talks about people being given the opportunity to leave, whether that's a form of intimidation or not. She's just a researcher for the Office of the Prosecutor. She doesn't have that kind of expertise. Although things like this sometimes go to weight, I think in this case that particular observation is outside of the expertise of the witness and shouldn't be allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. But as you indicated, it all goes to the weight and credibility, but the witness must have heard it. Thank you for your intervention, Mr. Robinson. Let's proceed, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, yesterday you also -- Wednesday you were also shown -- no, I showed that to you. I'm sorry. Could I have 65 ter 01217. And yesterday -- Wednesday, again, Mr. Karadzic was talking to you about these temporary transfers. This is a report of the work on the Municipal Assembly and the War Presidency from the 1st of January, 1992, to the 20th of April, 1993, and this is something that you cite in your report at footnote 9, 69, 115, 136 and 170. In this report, do the Muslim -- I'm sorry, the municipal authorities, the War Presidency, discuss the temporary or otherwise evacuation of its population, the non-Serb population?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's where I got the quotation from that I read earlier about the -- being offered either to organise their own evacuation or have it carried out by the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could scroll to -- and this is, I think, at footnote 170 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- which is on page 5 of the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It says that it would be a temporary transfer, but certain areas were an exception and dealt with militarily. However, as I mentioned before, the Assembly deputy, Miro Vjestica, did say he hoped the Muslims would not return.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask Ms. Sutherland to present the entire document to the Chamber, or, alternatively, ask to get more time myself. Let's see, on the first page in Serbian, what happened in Arapusa the day before and the reason for this decision about temporary resettlement, because it's explicitly said that it's temporary. Equally, if the document is admitted, it should be admitted in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are admitting it in its entirety, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2739, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago that Vjestica formed his view on the population?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recall his speech he made at the Assembly session?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Which Assembly decision was that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th of May, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 0026 -- no, it's a P number. P01379. Sorry, P00956. And if we could go to English page 20 to 21, and in B/C/S, the page is 16 to 18, where we can see Vjestica beginning to speak on page 20 of the English and page 16 of the B/C/S. And then if I can perhaps direct you to page 21 in the English and 18 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The quotation I was thinking of, it's at the very bottom of the screen. Oops. Yeah, it's between the two pages. That there are no more Muslims left in the Serbian Municipality of Krupa, and now that they have heard the president has told us --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask for the reference in the B/C/S text. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The quote is on page 18 -- page 17, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we go back to the previous page in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, page 17.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's -- for the interpreters, it's in the middle of the large paragraph, so it's about one-third of the way down the page. He lists various settlements, and then he says: [Interpretation] "Will I have anywhere -- will they have anywhere to go back to? I don't think so." [In English] So at the very bottom of the English page, it says: "Will they have a place to return to?" And then the next page goes on: "I think it is unlikely after our president has told us the happy news that the right bank of the Una is the border." That's a reference to one of the strategic objectives establishing the Una as a border of the Republika Srpska. So he explicitly ties the inability of the Muslims to return to their homes as -- he explicitly ties that to the strategic objective of the border of the state.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And while we have that Assembly session, if we could go to page 17.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I also note something on that page? Well, sorry, it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You haven't asked me about it. There's a reference to Bosanski Novi, that an ultimatum has been issued for the Muslims to surrender their weapons, which is -- earlier, Dr. Karadzic was taking me through the report of the Crisis Staff and saying there was no ethnic criterion for their surrender, but, I think the Muslims will soon be disarmed there too, Vitnica is saying. Or that's in Sanski Most. So, Bosanski Novi, Sanski Most, it's the Muslims being disarmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could quickly go to, while we have this 12th Assembly session on the screen, to Mr. Kalinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you remember him making a speech at this Assembly? Mr. Karadzic took you yesterday to a document which was signed by him in English --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- saying that people had to --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Co-operate with the International Red Cross and humanitarian organisations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And -- yes, yes. If we could go to page 17 of the English and page 14 of the B/C/S. Are you familiar with what he said at this Assembly session?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know I've read it. I'm not quite sure what quotation -- or what passage you're leading me to now, but I've certainly read his speeches. Oh, I remember this, yes, where he says: "The enemy cannot be trusted, and until they are physically militarily destroyed and crushed, which, of course, implies eliminating and liquidating their key people." And he does not hesitate in selecting that option.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the document, I think, we saw from Mr. Karadzic was dated around the end of April. So this is a fortnight later. This is what Mr. Kalinic has to say about the matter?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this -- that seems to follow my recollection of the chronology.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could have 65 ter -- sorry, it's Exhibit P1379 on the screen. This is the 34th Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recall Mr. Vjestica speaking at this Assembly session?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know I've reviewed his speeches. I can't recall right now what he's saying, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could ask for page 20 of the English and page 18 of the B/C/S, just so that we can see Mr. Vjestica's name at the beginning of his speech. And then if we could go to page 22, the last paragraph on page 22, going over to page 23 in the B/C/S. And in English, the last paragraph on page 24, going over into page 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it starts around about the war in Krupa started on the 21st of April -- on 21 April?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then he's talking about Abdic --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Fikret Abdic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- coming to Krupa?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He describes one village as a Turkish village, by which he means Muslim. He's used the derogatory term "Turk" for Muslims here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then he says: "And, gentlemen, since it is written in this agreement that everyone will be able to go back to their own territory, that means that his people will be going back to Veliki Babic, and we will have to compensate everything we destroyed and burnt and 17 mosques that we flattened." Is that consistent with the proposal that you were shown in your evidence-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Klickovic's proposal from May 1992 to destroy settlements.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's the 25th of May, 1992, and it's Exhibit P02616?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it indicates that although they have a written agreement that everyone will be able to go back, they hadn't really planned on it, and that's why they destroyed everything. And Dr. Karadzic right away says he was always charmed by Vjestica, admires his fighting spirit, but nothing is true of what he just said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could leave that document now. Mr. Karadzic took you, at transcript page 14729 to 14736, to an Exhibit D01338, which was minutes of a meeting held in Bosanski Petrovac on the 3rd of June, 1992. I don't want to go back to Petrovac, but he suggested to you that the municipality was being put under pressure from the masses, who were not getting paid to sack the non-Serb workers. And you responded at transcript page 14736: "I see that this is one member, he's saying that was the reason, but I know the ARK was taking a similar position from above." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 01095, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a decision by Brdjanin, dated the 22nd of June, 1992, that: "Only personnel of Serbian ethnicity may hold executive posts, posts where the information flow is possible ..." Is this the decision that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this decision seems to come after the one in Petrovac, but I was certainly -- if this is what I had in mind, I see it implemented in municipalities, and it may be that there were earlier versions of these instructions. But certainly at the time, at this time in June, they're implementing these decisions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if we go to the next page, we can see the document for immediate delivery to the president of the Municipal Crisis Staff. And then the following page, page 3, where we have the president of the Prijedor Crisis Staff, Milomir Stakic, on the 23rd of June --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Receiving and forwarding this decision of ARK.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is that consistent with what you have in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If we could go back one page, too, I would note another interesting item that they -- reference to the Serbs had to vote in the plebiscite to prove their loyalty. That's something else that I note in my report, the participation in the plebiscite as an indicator of loyalty, and that they must regard the SDS as the sole representative of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2740, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, if we can very quickly look at Exhibit P0008, which is a communication dated the 25th of June, 1992, from Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's implementing the steps and decisions set out in the Crisis Staff decision that we just saw; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says employees have already been sacked, and the remaining ones have now been sacked, except for one, who, when he finishes his tasks, will be fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour. Sorry, it's already an exhibit. I'd like to take you to another example of crisis staffs making decisions in relation to the non-Serb population, and that's 65 ter 05752.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is a decision of the Prijedor Crisis Staff on the release of imprisoned persons, dated the 2nd of June, 1992. And can you just very briefly tell the Chamber the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cite it in my report as an example of how the crisis staffs were deciding about who would be imprisoned or released. I find Article 1 quite significant, that all Serbs who have been imprisoned by mistake are to be released, implying that there was an ethnic criterion for the imprisonment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2741, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: May I ask, could we work today a little bit longer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You could have asked that later on, but let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I now want to ask you a few questions about -- and show you a few documents about the Kotor Varos municipality. If I could have 65 ter 0338 on the screen, please. Mr. Karadzic painted the Kotor Varos municipality as one of the authorities having everything under control, so to speak, and I just want to -- for you to see whether, in this document, that's really the case in Kotor Varos at the end of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Objection. Leading and comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, what's the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Dr. Karadzic brought it to my attention, showing the -- that Serb houses were being burned in Kotor. I recall that he described Kotor Varos as Serb territory, and described Muslim and Croat enclaves as deep in the heart of Serb territory. I -- after I checked what I had before on my -- in my information on Kotor Varos population, I don't know if that's something I could mention or not, but to declare it a Serb territory is a bit of a stretch. He's -- it shows -- if you could direct me to which passage you want my attention. He describes the police describing problems with the special unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's Dr. Gajanin?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in general. But, yes, he was driven away from the Health Centre by members of the special unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And do you know whether there were any people killed at the Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes. I believe there was -- it was one of the killing sites, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And was anything done by the authorities in Kotor Varos about the special unit that came to Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they requested that the ARK or CSB in Banja Luka withdraw them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And did that happen?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar, I'm sorry, with the sequence of events regarding the special unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It says here that Djekanovic said last night that he had told Dubocanin -- do you know what Dubocanin is being referred to there?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: A member of the ARK crisis staff, I believe. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that Slobodan Dubocanin?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: About everything going on at the Health Centre and in the town, he said that: "All these questions had to cleared up and information provided on the behaviour of the members of the special unit at the meeting with S. Zupljanin, the chief of the CSB, scheduled for tomorrow?" And you said that they had asked -- the crisis staff asked for these special units to be removed?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly asked to slow down and pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My apologies. Yes, that's as I recall. I've read a lot of minutes from a lot of municipalities, and I can't sort out the sequence of events without some reference to the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2742, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Finally, I just want to show you one document, and that -- Mr. Karadzic took you to quite a number of documents, Crisis Staff minutes, for the period the 25th of October to the 2nd of November, and then the 3rd of November, the 7th, the 10th to the 12th of November, and this was all in relation to Vecici. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you mentioned at page 14658 to 14659, he asked you about Vecici, and you said your understanding of it was that it was surrounded by Serbian forces and that, in the end, some killings followed in early November, but you can't honestly remember whether they were the men of this village or another place, in a school. Mr. Karadzic didn't take you to the War Presidency minutes of the 6th of November, 1992. And if I could have 65 ter 00292 on the screen, please. What's Mr. Djekanovic up to on this day, what he's reporting?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's going to Grabovica, monitoring the cleaning-up of the terrain and the cleaning of the school. And my understanding is that there was a massacre in the school, and there's the president of the War Presidency making sure it's being cleaned up.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do we know this? How do we know this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That question was about to be asked by me. How do you know that a massacre took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's -- it's not in these pages, I know, but I just know from the Krajisnik trial, the -- my -- the investigations into the killings scheduled in Krajisnik of that. It's beyond the scope of my report, but I don't know when I can bring in what has been established by other trials or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could see 65 ter 00719 -- sorry, 00293.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a one -- a report from the 1 KK, the 1st Krajina Corps, to the Republika Srpska Army Main Staff, a regular combat report for the 4th of November, 1992. And they talk about their -- about 40 Green Berets, members were killed, and about 200 were captured. A brutal massacre of the captured members of the Green Berets started because of a wounding of four and a killing of one soldier. Is this what you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that document be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the link with the school? It says: "I'll undertake measures to prevent ...," but what does it have to do with the school?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why do you suggest it to be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I can seek to tender it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: But why did you seek it to be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, because when I asked Ms. Hanson was this what she was referring to, she said, I think so. At least that's how I understood it. But if I may take her to one more document, Your Honour, 65 ter 00722. This is another combat report from the following day, where it states: "The deaths of those captured from Vecici were simply the result of combat activities in the clash against the VRS following the death of one soldier and the wounding of several others, and it seems to be downgraded now to more than 150 extremists died in combat." Yes: "In the clash against the VRS, following the death of one soldier and the wounding of several others, more than 150 extremists died in combat." No, Your Honour, we're still not getting the link to the Grbavica school. We'll have to get that through the military expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you seek to tender those documents at a later stage or now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can either mark them for identification now or we can tender them now, and the military expert will speak to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether that link has been sufficiently shown at this moment. I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you tender them at a later stage, Ms. Sutherland, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Karadzic, you wanted to ask further questions. But please explain to us what questions you are going to ask and why it --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And tell us why it was not -- it could not have been raised before, and in what context it arose from the re-examination of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is precisely what I am going to explain. My learned friend, Madam Sutherland, has just been given a new direct examination. 14641 and 14642 are the pages where she did that. Actually, it is the pages on which I said, and Madam Sutherland misinterpreted: [In English] Hanson: "Crisis staffs and war presidencies as the institutions through which the moving out of the population was to be organised, including the signing over of property. So I don't mean simply the ARK and so on. I also see them as many individual municipalities." Karadzic: "We will get back to this issue of property being signed over. This is what you are reading into this, but this was not done, this was not implemented. You don't know that, but this was not implemented." [Interpretation] There are two things at stake here. What is being implied is that crisis staffs were formed up and were instrumental in the forcible resettlement of the population, and that their assets and property were taken away from them. And based on that, Madam Sutherland had been given the chance to re-examine and introduce new elements, including demographic elements that did not arise either from my cross-examination, as a whole, or from these particular two pages and the answers that the witness provided in cross-examination. As for the agencies, they are services, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Do you find the reference to the transcript pages of today, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Whether you can find the page numbers of the transcript Mr. Karadzic just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that the Agency -- the Agency for Resettlement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, referring to his comment that that was not implemented.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never contested the existence of the agencies. What I challenge is the implication that they implemented the forcible resettlement of the population and confiscation of property. And this is what was interpreted on those ten lines, and those ten lines were the very base for the additional questions by the Prosecutor. The document I showed after that, 1308, demonstrated that there was a reason for me to ask those questions, and now we have opened an entirely new page in the whole process.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the transcript pages was 14640 to 14642, so it would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I meant in today's transcript. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, from today's transcript, that's at page 59, if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The way I read Wednesday's transcript, Mr. Karadzic was disputing they were implementing -- or, in fact, that -- the very fact that the resettlement agencies were implemented in the ARK or, in fact, anywhere in Bosnia, and that's why I took him -- Ms. Hanson to all these documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- to show that there was a resettlement agency and it was working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we are going to give extra burden to you, Ms. Hanson. We are minded whether we should have a more informed decision on this issue. So probably you may be free of your obligation to the office of the Prosecutor, but given that you are still here, could you come by on Monday morning, and we'll issue a decision first thing on Monday. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Reid advises me that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll deal with it on Monday, then. Yes, please. I thought you were raising the items, telling us --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No. It was just one English translation that's been up-loaded, but that doesn't matter. It can wait until Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. We rise for the week, and we'll resume on Monday morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 20th day of June, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.30 p.m.,
